key_insight: Augment code-generating LLMs with an online repository memory that records project history, APIs, conventions, and reviewer feedback so generated pull requests are 'organic'—aligned with a repo's implicit architecture and more likely to be accepted.
problem_solved: LLM-based coding agents produce functionally plausible changes that maintainers reject because they ignore project-specific conventions, duplicate internal APIs, or violate long-evolved architectural constraints. The paper addresses how to make automated PRs fit repository-specific norms and workflows.
method: Construct an online repository memory that indexes commits, API signatures, usage patterns, tests, CI results, PR discussions, and code-owner metadata for retrieval.

Use retrieval-augmented generation: condition the LLM on relevant memory slices (historical examples, canonical APIs, style snippets) to propose diffs and PR descriptions that respect local conventions.
Close the loop with continual updates: ingest new commits, reviewer feedback, and CI outcomes to refresh memory and bias future proposals toward accepted patterns.
impact: Makes automated code contributions practical and trustworthy by increasing PR acceptance, reducing maintainer overhead, and enabling LLMs to respect long-lived, project-specific design constraints—critical for real-world deployment of code generation tools.

paper_title: Learning to Commit: Generating Organic Pull Requests via Online Repository Memory
paper_authors: Mo Li, L. H. Xu, Qitai Tan, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu
